All new home battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 24 months after this standard takes effect. parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving fire, smoke, or uncontrolled overheating to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a full incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 48 hours, provide immediate safety instructions, and notify customers of nearby units if the incident may indicate a hazard shared by those units. Suspected incidents must be investigated and reported; uncertainty is not grounds to delay initial notice.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving fire, smoke, or uncontrolled overheating to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a full incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 48 hours, provide immediate safety instructions, and notify customers of nearby units if the incident may indicate a hazard shared by those units. Suspected incidents must be investigated and reported; uncertainty is not grounds to delay initial notice.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving fire, smoke, or uncontrolled overheating to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a full incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 48 hours, provide immediate safety instructions, and notify customers of nearby units if the incident may indicate a hazard shared by those units. Reports must include known injuries, property damage, model and serial number, and corrective actions. Suspected incidents must be investigated and reported; uncertainty is not grounds to delay initial notice. Manufacturers must maintain records of thermal incidents and reconcile those records against service, warranty, and customer-support records at least annually; any newly identified reportable incident must be reported promptly under these deadlines.

[Customers:] provide the relevant model's results directly to customers who buy or own that model. S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved sample size and test protocol. No more than 5% of tested units of any model may fail. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective actions to regulators, and provide the relevant model’s results directly to customers who buy or own that model. These customer disclosures do not require public publication of individual-company per-model failure rates. S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All new home battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 24 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must retrofit compatible capability to already-installed units within six years of the effective date, or document to the regulator why a unit cannot safely be retrofitted and provide an equivalent protective measure.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new home battery systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 24 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must retrofit compatible capability to already-installed units within six years of the effective date, or document to the regulator why a unit cannot safely be retrofitted and provide an equivalent protective measure. Shut-off must be operable by the customer and accessible to emergency responders under defined emergency procedures, with safeguards against unauthorized activation.

parameters.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted. The suppression system must be suitable for the battery chemistry and installation, and must be tested to a regulator-approved protocol. Manufacturers must provide installation, inspection, and maintenance instructions to customers. This requirement does not replace other required fire-safety measures.

parameters.quote: Notices must be sent promptly and through direct channels where available. A recall is mandatory when any model's thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy, including repair, replacement, or refund.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Notices must be sent promptly and through direct channels where available. A recall is mandatory when any model's thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy, including repair, replacement, or refund.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must give customers clear safety notices upon learning of a credible model-specific hazard, including the hazard, affected models and serial ranges, immediate precautions, and where to obtain updates and assistance. Notices must be sent promptly and through direct channels where available; public notices must also be issued when affected units cannot be reliably identified or reached. A recall is mandatory when any model’s thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and provide an effective remedy, including repair, replacement, or refund. The regulator shall verify incident counts and installed-unit denominators; verification must not delay interim protective notices or action where there is an immediate risk.

judge_section_notes: S2 keeps the 5% limit and bars public per-model publication, but sales never have to stop: the regulator may restrict sales, so a model above 5% such as Hearth 10 (6.2%) can keep selling during corrective action. S5 imposes a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition or interim trigger, which directly reaches Ember 8 (9.9); S3 gives new units 24 months and retrofits 72 months, which is weaker than the 12-month new-unit benchmark. S1 is the strongest section, with 24-hour reporting of all thermal incidents that applies to both companies' unreported incidents.
